source.title: The LZ78 Source
source.authors: Naomi Sagan; A. Dembo; Matthew Ho; T. Weissman

page_placements.theme: Data structure, depth and architecture set ICL emergence and in-context loss profiles in small models

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures in-context loss behavior under different data priors, model depths, and training durations, providing a conceptual test of whether in-context learning depends on the data and setup. It does not identify or measure induction heads.
record.gate_note: The study reports ICL-related loss behavior on synthetic LZ78-source data and genomic data. It does not measure induction heads, their formation, or a training-loss bump. Referenced findings from other papers are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The study trains small NanoGPT transformers (1–5 layers) on LZ78-source data. It uses the original's ICL criterion: loss falling over the context. It never identifies, measures or ablates induction heads or previous-token heads. It tracks no head formation, loss bump or ICL transience. Induction heads appear only in cited related work ([13]–[15]). Its results are on a related construct: whether in-context loss decrease appears, by depth, prior and training steps. They do not cover whether or when induction heads form, or whether ICL persists. That finding goes under fits_no_version, not V5.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors' ICL experiments are an 'initial exploration' giving insight into the potential and limits of transformer ICL on non-Markovian data. Deeper models and longer training show loss falling over the context; a large gap to the true log probability remains; behaviour varies with the prior, and there is qualitative transfer to genomic data. They draw no conclusions about induction heads.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains small transformers on LZ78-source data and evaluates their loss behavior; it does not reproduce the original induction-head identification or mechanistic analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported ICL loss behavior varies with source prior, transformer depth, training progress, and whether evaluation uses synthetic or genomic data.

fits_no_version.finding: Context-wise loss decrease (Olsson-style ICL) is absent in 1–2 layer models and in a 4-layer model early in training (500 steps). It is present in 3–5 layer models after training on Jeffreys-prior LZ78 data. It is less clear under the higher-entropy Dirichlet(2,2) prior. Under the almost-degenerate prior it appears only late, after about 4000 steps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Emergence of in-context learning (loss falling with token index) in small transformers depends on depth, training duration and the training source's entropy or dependency structure, independent of any head-level mechanism.

record.problems: Transformer experiments cover depths 1–5 and only 5 epochs; the authors report limited computational resources and note that longer training or larger models may change results. Most plotted comparisons have no numerical values or uncertainty estimates in the text. The study does not analyze attention heads, so its loss results cannot establish an induction-head mechanism.
record.rows_left_out: No separately described numerical outcomes for the figures were available in the text; figure-only curve values were not transcribed. Comparisons with μk, CTW, the LZ78 SPA, and source log probability were included only where the text explicitly connected them to the ICL behavior or a condition-dependent result.

untested.parts: No attention-head analysis, no previous-token composition, no [A][B]…[A]→[B] copying.
No head-formation timing, no training-loss bump, no phase-change analysis. Only checkpoints at 500 and 4000 steps are described qualitatively.
No large models; no attribution of ICL to induction heads.
Induction behaviour is not measured in any model or architecture.
Does not measure whether or when induction heads form, or whether ICL persists or fades with training. Only the presence of ICL loss decrease by depth, prior and steps is reported.
No comparison of induction heads with other mechanisms; no few-shot task learning.
No analysis of formation sub-steps or multiple transitions.

missing.what: Depth ablation under the almost-degenerate prior: 1-layer ≈ µ1, 2-layer between µ3 and µ5, 3-layer ≈ µ11, and 4–5 layers surpass µ13.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' with V5 links is rejected. The study never measures induction heads, and V5's ICL clause concerns whether ICL persists, which is not studied. ICL presence alone is a related construct. Results are qualitative from figures, with no numbers or uncertainty, training is limited to 5 epochs, and the work is peer-reviewed in IEEE Trans. IT.

versions.untested_parts: Does not analyze attention heads, previous-token-head composition, or the [A][B] … [A] → [B] copying mechanism.
Does not measure induction-head formation or test whether it coincides with an abrupt ICL gain and a bump in training loss.
Does not attribute most ICL in large transformers to induction heads or test large transformers.
Does not test induction behavior across model families, or across other architectures or modalities.
Tests whether ICL loss behavior varies with data prior, depth, and training duration; does not test whether induction heads form, or when they form.
Does not distinguish few-shot task learning from repeated-token copying or compare induction heads with other mechanisms.
Does not examine induction-head formation or test whether it consists of multiple transitions.

rows.subject: one-layer transformer
rows.operation_detail: Trained on LZ78-source sequences under the Jeffreys prior and evaluated on held-out sequences; measured cumulative normalized log loss across context.
rows.measure: Cumulative normalized log loss over context; whether it decreases with context.
rows.value: Log loss increases over the context; over the full sequence, performs only as well as CTW with depth D = 1.
rows.note: The authors say this model does not display the described ICL loss-decrease property.
rows.check: Measures context-wise loss decrease (ICL) only; no induction-head measurement, so it does not bear on V5's head-formation or ICL-persistence claim.

rows.subject: five-layer transformer
rows.stage_stated: trained on LZ78-source data for 5 epochs
rows.operation_detail: Trained on LZ78-source sequences under a Dirichlet(2, 2) prior and evaluated on held-out sequences; measured loss curves.
rows.measure: Loss behavior over context and during learning, as described by the authors.
rows.value: Loss curves do not smoothly decrease during learning, even for the five-layer transformer; the authors nevertheless state that some ICL occurs, but less than under the Jeffreys prior.
rows.note: The text does not give a numerical loss value or specify a sharp transition; it reports weaker and less smooth ICL than under the Jeffreys prior.
rows.check: Authors infer weaker ICL indirectly from comparison with CTW and µk, not from a measured context-wise decrease.

rows.subject: two-layer transformer
rows.stage_stated: trained on LZ78-source data for 5 epochs
rows.operation_detail: Trained on LZ78-source sequences under a Dirichlet(2, 2) prior and evaluated on held-out sequences; compared its log loss with the three-layer model.
rows.measure: Log loss compared across model depths.
rows.baseline: three-layer transformer, which had slightly higher log loss
rows.value: Slightly lower log loss than the three-layer transformer.
rows.note: The paper attributes the difference tentatively to the three-layer model becoming stuck in a local minimum; this comparison alone does not establish context-wise loss decrease.
rows.check: Compares overall log loss across depths (2- vs 3-layer). This is not an ICL or induction-head measure and arguably should not be a row.

rows.subject: four- and five-layer transformers (aggregate as reported)
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated on genomic data; the authors report that the larger transformers recover CTW-like performance and appear to learn in-context.
rows.measure: In-context learning behavior, as inferred from the reported genomic-data evaluation.
rows.value: The authors say the models appear to be learning in-context; they recover CTW-like performance on this data.
rows.note: Reported for the pair; the paper calls the genomic-data results inconclusive.
rows.check: Authors call the Figure 14 genomic results inconclusive. The ICL inference rests on CTW-like performance, not a measured decrease.

rows.value: The log loss increases toward the end of the context up until 4000 training steps.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: The introduction cites induction-head findings, and the experiments cite the original's context-wise loss criterion. Induction heads are neither analyzed nor used as a tool.

tranche.reason: The experiments measure context-wise loss and predictive performance, without identifying induction heads, measuring their formation, or testing ICL persistence. They do not test any listed claim version.

source_check.notes: Row states describe the reported ICL loss patterns only; none establishes an induction-head result. Under Dirichlet(2, 2), weaker ICL is inferred indirectly from predictor comparisons rather than a clear context-wise loss decrease.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Across data priors, depths, and training progress
reader_labels.reason: The reported ICL loss pattern is not uniform: it is absent for shallow models and an early four-layer checkpoint, weaker under Dirichlet(2, 2), and changes during training under the almost-degenerate prior (r1, r2, r4, r9, r12).
